Residential site to go out for tender
body:
The Government will put a site in Shek Mun, Shatin out for tender for private residential development, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said today.

 

The tender was announced as part of the land sale programme for the third-quarter of 2026-27, and will run from this month until December.

 

The site is located at the junction of Tai Chung Kiu Road and On Sum Street. It has a floor space of around 48,090 sq m and can provide around 960 flats.

 

Ms Linn explained that the site is situated in a mature residential neighbourhood. Close to MTR Shek Mun Station, it has comprehensive surrounding infrastructure.

 

Originally zoned for commercial use, the site has received planning approval from the Town Planning Board for private residential development. Any approved developer will be requited to set aside some floor space to provide a public car park.

 

Other sources of private housing in this quarter’s land programme include the Urban Renewal Authority’s To Kwa Wan Road project, which is estimated to provide around 1,050 flats.

 

As for private development and redevelopment projects, seven are expected to complete lease modification or land exchange procedures in the third quarter, providing a total supply of around 1,835 flats. Ms Linn said this demonstrates developers’ optimistic market outlook.

 

Taking all sources of land supply into account, the total private housing land supply in the third quarter of this financial year will support the development of around 3,845 units.

 

Ms Linn said: “Together with the supply from the first two quarters of this financial year, the total private housing land supply in the first three quarters of this financial year is expected to support some 15,680 units, which has already exceeded our annual target of private housing supply, ie 12,600 units.”

 

Ms Linn said the Government will nevertheless continue to roll out land to the market.

 

She explained: “Firstly, the annual supply target is not a rigid indicator; the Government has all along evaluated the pace and trend of market supply in its totality from a macro perspective.

 

“Secondly, some development projects co-ordinated by the Government, e.g. the Northern Metropolis, railway property development and urban renewal projects, have their own specific timeframes in meeting the Government’s policy needs and the holistic development of their respective areas.

 

“Thirdly, with the generally positive market sentiment, there is sufficient demand and capacity for developers to take on mature urban land. The Government will continue to assess the circumstances and roll out land flexibly according to policy needs and market conditions."

 

In addition, the Development Bureau plans to put up for tender a Siu Lek Yuen site in Shatin for student hostel development this quarter. It is estimated the project will provide around 600 beds.

 

Ms Linn remarked that the site is near MTR City One Station and MTR Shek Mun Station, as well as post-secondary educational institutions.

title: 12 lease modifications logged in Q3
body:
The Lands Department announced today that it registered 12 lease modifications, two land exchanges and one lot extension in the Land Registry during the quarter ending September, generating a total land premium of approximately $2.934 billion.

 

Among the 15 registered transactions, two were technical changes involving no premium.

 

Five are located on Hong Kong Island, seven are in Kowloon and three are in the New Territories.

 

Another seven lots were granted by private treaty during the period.

 

One was granted to the government-owned Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company Limited for the development of an industry park, two were granted to the Housing Authority for public housing developments, and the remaining four were located in the Loop, Shek O, Yuen Long and Hung Hom.

title: Ngau Tam Mei land to be resumed
body:
The Lands Department today posted the first batch of resumption notices and acquisition notices for the development of the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area (NTM NDA).

 

Under the Lands Resumption Ordinance, a total of 1,043 private lots, covering an area of about 62 hectares, will be resumed for the project.

 

In addition, government land occupied by 23 graves and 22 urns, and covering an area of about 450 sq m, as well as land occupied by 27 fishponds, totalling 2,700 sq m, will be acquired under the Land Acquisition (Possessory Title) Ordinance.

 

All of the land will officially revert to the Government on January 16.

 

The department will post notices in areas concerned about three months before the departure deadlines for affected parties. It estimates that those affected will need to move out starting from the second quarter of 2027 at the earliest.

 

The NTM NDA represents the fifth NDA development to be launched within the Northern Metropolis. It will be developed alongside the San Tin Technopole as part of the San Tin University Town under an integrated town-planning concept.

 

The campus area in the NTM NDA is about 52 hectares. This includes an area of about five hectares reserved for the construction of Hong Kong's third medical school.

 

Site formation and infrastructure works for the NTM NDA are scheduled to commence in the first half of next year. “Spade-ready sites” will be available progressively starting from the end of 2028.

title: CE meets President of AIIB
body:
Chief Executive John Lee met President of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) Zou Jiayi at Government House today to exchange views on further strengthening regional financial co-operation.

 

Mr Lee welcomed Ms Zou and her delegation to the city to attend the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting 2026.

 

Noting that the AIIB has all along supported developing economies in improving infrastructure and promoting sustainable economic development, he said that Hong Kong, as a member of the AIIB, has been actively supporting its work.

 

He stated that with the announcement of Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the Policy Address last month, Hong Kong will continue to consolidate and enhance its financial strengths and strengthen development in areas including green finance, financial technology and offshore Renminbi business, which will help support the AIIB's project financing, fundraising and financial management to promote the sustainable development of infrastructure in Asia.

 

Mr Lee highlighted that Hong Kong is one of the world's leading international financial centres. It continues to come first as the world's freest economy and ranks third globally and first in Asia in the Global Financial Centres Index.

 

With its vibrant capital market, world-class professional services and diversified financial products, Hong Kong is well placed to provide flexible capital allocation support for the AIIB's projects such as those relating to carbon neutrality and green economic transformation.

 

Mr Lee added that the AIIB's issuance of Hong Kong dollar bonds in Hong Kong in recent years is a testament to the achievements of financial co-operation between the two sides. He welcomed the AIIB's continued use of Hong Kong's strengths as an international financial hub and its mature and comprehensive bond market to connect with investors around the world and empower projects with added value.

 

The Chief Executive said he is pleased that the AIIB will soon establish in Hong Kong an office serving both financing and operational functions, demonstrating the city's role as a gateway connecting the country and the world. He believes that the establishment of the office will create more opportunities for the local financial sector and deepen co-operation and exchanges between the two sides.

 

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will fully support the establishment and operation of the office, giving full play to Hong Kong's role as a "super connector" and "super value-adder" to facilitate the AIIB's business expansion, he added.

 

Mr Lee expressed the hope that both sides will continue to work together to strengthen collaboration in areas such as transition finance, technology and innovation and talent development to jointly promote regional economic prosperity.

 

Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui also attended the meeting.

title: FS wraps up Thai visit
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan concluded his visit to Bangkok, Thailand this morning after meeting with Thai Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Ekniti Nitithanprapas.

 

During the meeting in the morning, Mr Chan and  Ekniti Nitithanprapas exchanged views on further strengthening economic, trade and financial co-operation between Hong Kong and Thailand.

 

The two sides explored ways to deepen co-operation and connect foreign direct investment in Thailand with Hong Kong's capital market to further support enterprises investing and expanding their businesses in Thailand.

 

Mr Chan said that Hong Kong could leverage its strengths as an international financial centre to provide comprehensive investment and financing support for enterprises in Thailand. Hong Kong also welcomed closer regulatory co-operation between the two securities markets to encourage dual listings by enterprises from both places and strengthen capital market ties.

 

He added that with Mainland enterprises accelerating their international expansion and increasing investment in Thailand and Southeast Asia, Hong Kong could further enhance its bridging role by matching the Mainland's technological strengths with Thailand's industrial development needs, thereby fostering investment and industrial co-operation.

 

Mr Chan thanked Mr Ekniti for visiting Hong Kong to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting, and invited him to attend the Asian Financial Forum in Hong Kong in January next year to further strengthen economic, trade and financial ties between the two places and across the region, and jointly explore new opportunities for co-operation.

 

The Financial Secretary also met with the chief executive officer and senior management of a major French bank with extensive operations in Hong Kong this morning.

 

They exchanged views on developments in the fixed income and currency markets in Hong Kong and the region, green and sustainable finance, tokenised financial products, and asset and wealth management.

 

Mr Chan welcomed the group's continued expansion in Hong Kong and its use of the city as a key hub for developing its regional business, tapping into the opportunities offered by Hong Kong as an international financial centre.

 

Having concluded his morning programme, Mr Chan departed for Hong Kong and returned this afternoon.

title: FS attends Thai meetings
body:
As a member of the Chinese delegation, Financial Secretary Paul Chan today attended the plenary session of the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group (WBG) in Bangkok, Thailand.

 

Mr Chan also took part in discussions organised by financial media and a think tank, met senior executives of international financial institutions and enterprises, and hosted a dinner for financial leaders.

 

At a fireside chat organised by Bloomberg, Mr Chan outlined how Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan, providing clear development directions and goals for the public and businesses.

 

He said that Hong Kong would focus on developing its “four centres and one hub”, thereby reinforcing and enhancing its status as an international financial, shipping and trade centre. He said Hong Kong would also leverage its strengths and work in tandem with other cities in the Greater Bay Area to advance its development as an innovation and technology (I&T) centre.

 

Mr Chan stressed that financial development must serve the real economy, adding that Hong Kong will deepen its “Finance+” strategy to empower different industries, support enterprises in their upgrading and transformation efforts, and provide venture capital, patient capital and long-term funding for I&T to accelerate the development of emerging industries.

 

He remarked that Hong Kong’s international character is a core strength that must be continuously reinforced and enhanced. While strengthening ties with mature markets such as Europe and the US and attracting international capital, Hong Kong will also deepen co-operation with emerging markets in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Central Asia. Mr Chan elaborated that Hong Kong will open up two-way investment opportunities by bringing together capital and industries to meet development needs across these markets.

 

Beyond promoting business and trade exchanges, he said, Hong Kong will leverage its strengths in financial and professional services, including green and sustainable finance and trade finance, to support infrastructure, supply chain and industrial development in the region.

 

On the topic of offshore renminbi business, Mr Chan said Hong Kong is expanding its range of investment products, enhancing custody and collateral management infrastructure, and increasing liquidity to add depth and breadth to the market.

 

He stressed that “one country, two systems” provides Hong Kong with an institutional advantage in its long-term development, adding that talent is a key driving force for its future growth.

 

He said Hong Kong will remain free, open, diverse and inclusive, welcoming enterprises and talent from around the world to set up and pursue careers in the city, and young people to study in it.

 

Mr Chan also took part in a broadcast fireside chat hosted by the Atlantic Council, a US think tank.

 

He described the latest developments in Hong Kong’s financial markets and how its first five-year plan will advance I&T, promote the integrated development of education, technology, talent and industries in the Northern Metropolis, and deepen co-operation with other bay area cities in I&T industries.

 

In addition, Mr Chan met WBG Managing Director and Chief Administrative Officer Zhang Wencai for an exchange of views on the global and regional economic outlook and deepening co-operation between Hong Kong and the WBG.

 

Mr Chan also met the management of a major European digital bank to discuss fintech development, digital banking services and cross-boundary payments, and outlined opportunities in Hong Kong’s financial markets.

 

In the evening, Mr Chan attended a dinner organised by the Hong Kong Economic & Trade Office in Bangkok. He spoke of developments in Hong Kong’s economy and financial services sector, and discussed opportunities to strengthen financial co-operation.

title: AI assistant added to iAM Smart
body:
The Digital Policy Office announced today that an AI Assistant feature is being introduced in the latest version of the “iAM Smart” mobile application to answer enquiries about government services.

 

The update will be rolled out gradually via official application stores from today through to late October.

 

The AI Assistant's service covers enquiries related to public services provided by the Government. Members of the public can type in queries and the assistant will retrieve information instantly from official sources, and organise it into coherent and concise content, using AI technology. 

 

When users enquire about an online application procedure, the AI Assistant will list out eligibility criteria, step-by-step instructions and a relevant service link, enabling one-click access to the online service. Where applicable, it will also integrate with the "e-ME" form-filling function of “iAM Smart” to assist users in completing online forms.

 

To activate the AI Assistant, users can simply update to the latest version of the app and tap the icon of the mascot "Swifty" on the homepage.

 

An enhanced version of the AI Assistant with personalised features will be launched before the end of the year.

title: Accelerator applications supported
body:
The Innovation & Technology Commission announced today that the Pilot Innovation & Technology Accelerator Scheme Assessment Committee, under the Innovation & Technology Fund, has given its support in principle to a batch of nine applications.

 

The list of applicants supported is as follows: BJ-HK-SZ Innotech Accelerator; China Outbound Accelerator; China Resources Corporate Services (HK); Hong Kong Branch of The National Torch Academy of Innovation & Entrepreneurship Co.; Surrich Consulting Co.; Tenwings Accelevator Company; ventureLAB Smart City Accelerator; Xi'an Jiaotong University Hong Kong Institute of Advanced Studies Co.; and Zhong Xing No.1 Investment Fund.

 

Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Prof Sun Dong said that the nine organisations possess extensive networks and resources in areas such as artificial intelligence, robotics, biomedicine, new energy and new materials.

 

“They will provide value-added services including co-working space, research and development support, investment matching and market development to accelerate the growth of innovation and technology (I&T) companies in Hong Kong.

 

“The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will continue to enhance the I&T ecosystem and develop Hong Kong into an international I&T centre.”

 

The scheme aims to attract I&T enterprise service providers which have proven track records in and beyond Hong Kong to set up accelerator bases in the city and support the development and of I&T enterprises.

 

Under the scheme, the Government will provide funding support on a one‑to‑two matching basis in relation to service providers, with a ceiling subsidy of $30 million. The project duration is up to three years.

 

The scheme has received over 50 applications since launching in January. The nine organisations were selected for funding support based on a series of assessment criteria, including their levels of experience, operational models, capital and resources, the quality of their management and project teams, and expected benefits to Hong Kong’s I&T ecosystem.

 

Call 3543 5904 or send an email for enquiries.

title: FS concludes Nanjing visit
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan today concluded his visit to Nanjing by meeting the leadership of Jiangsu Province and touring advanced manufacturing and pharmaceutical enterprises.

 

Mr Chan began the day with a breakfast meeting with member of the Standing Committee of the CPC Jiangsu Provincial Committee and Executive Vice Governor of Jiangsu Province Zhang Wenbing to discuss deepening economic and trade co-operation, strengthening collaboration in innovation and technology (I&T), and supporting enterprises in their international expansion.

 

Mr Chan noted that the visit strengthened ties with the Jiangsu Provincial Government, universities, I&T institutions and enterprises, adding that Hong Kong will actively follow up on various co-operation projects to deliver more concrete results in Jiangsu-Hong Kong collaboration.

 

The delegation then visited a Jiangsu-based energy and energy-saving equipment enterprise to learn about its technology research and development (R&D), commercialisation of its research outcomes and its business development. They also toured a pharmaceutical company to examine its drug R&D, production methods and global marketing operations.

 

During the visits, Mr Chan emphasised that I&T remains a key area of co-operation between Jiangsu and Hong Kong. He highlighted that both regions have ample scope for collaboration in technology R&D, the commercialisation of research outcomes and international market expansion.

 

He added that both regions can further promote two-way investment and talent exchanges to foster deeper industrial integration.

 

Turning to innovative drugs, Mr Chan explained that enterprises can leverage Hong Kong's strengths in drug R&D and its reformed drug approval regime to accelerate market expansion.

 

The Financial Secretary encouraged both businesses to utilise Hong Kong's internationally connected capital markets, experience in meeting the highest international standards, high-quality professional services, and strengths as an international financial and talent hub to scale up in overseas markets.

title: HK debuts first 'sidecar' securities
body:
The Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau today welcomed the inaugural issuance of insurance-linked securities (ILS) in the form of a “sidecar” by the PICC Property & Casualty Company (PICC P&C) in Hong Kong.

 

With a size of US$12 million, equivalent to about HK$94 million, the “sidecar” issuance provides quota share reinsurance protection for offshore windfarm property insurance businesses on the Chinese Mainland.

 

Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui said: “We welcome PICC P&C’s issuance of Hong Kong’s first ‘sidecar’. This demonstrates Hong Kong’s combined strengths in reinsurance and capital markets.”

 

“The issuance marks significant progress gained for Hong Kong’s insurance industry and capital markets in risk transfer and the use of alternative capital under the support of our country. It will further enhance the market’s capacity to manage catastrophe and other specialty risks, and consolidate Hong Kong’s position as an international risk management centre,” Mr Hui added.

 

The financial services chief pointed out that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan has proposed fully leveraging Hong Kong’s competitive edge in the international insurance, reinsurance, and capital markets, to advance the synergised development of traditional insurance and non-traditional risk management tools.

 

“This will enable us to unleash the synergy effect of multilayered risk transfer and pooling mechanisms through ILS and other tools, thus consolidating our strategic role as a regional and global catastrophe and specialty risk management hub,” he said.

 

Ultimately, the proposal aims to support the National 15th Five-Year Plan which identifies the enhancement of the catastrophe risk protection framework and risk-pooling mechanisms as a key task.

 

“ILS and captive insurance, which we have long been promoting, can provide enterprises ‘going global’ with diversified means of spreading and managing risks," Mr Hui added.

 

“We expect this combination of financial policy measures will allow enterprises to leverage Hong Kong as a safe haven for 'going global' with greater ease of mind.”

title: FS promotes HK in Nanjing
body:
On the second day of a visit to Nanjing, Financial Secretary Paul Chan met Jiangsu provincial leaders and business representatives, attended a conference promoting support for enterprises in “going global”, and visited a platform for the commercialisation of research outcomes.

 

The visit by Mr Chan and his delegation aims to deepen co-operation between Jiangsu and Hong Kong, and support Mainland enterprises in leveraging Hong Kong to expand their global business.

 

In the morning, the finance chief attended a conference themed “Jiangsu-Hong Kong Partnership: Setting Sail Together”.

 

Addressing attendees, he highlighted that this year marks the beginning of the National 15th Five-Year Plan. Through closer co-operation, he remarked, Jiangsu and Hong Kong can seize the opportunities arising from the country’s pursuit of high-level opening up and translate these into tangible results for enterprises expanding into international markets.

 

He urged Jiangsu enterprises to use Hong Kong as a base for planning their global expansion.

 

Mr Chan also stressed that Jiangsu and Hong Kong enjoy a solid foundation of co-operation. Hong Kong is both Jiangsu’s largest source of foreign investment and its largest destination for outward investment. As of the end of September, 129 Jiangsu enterprises with a combined market capitalisation of about $1.44 trillion, were listed in Hong Kong.

 

The Financial Secretary said the two places have a sound basis for co-operation, with ample scope for further collaboration in innovation-driven development and expansion into international markets.

 

Mr Chan iterated that Hong Kong’s strengths extend beyond stock market listings and fundraising to its high concentration of international capital, financial institutions and professional talent. He said that enterprises can connect with international investors and partners through Hong Kong, broadening their financing channels to support business development at different stages.

 

On talent and innovation and technology (I&T), Mr Chan highlighted that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government is taking forward the development of the Northern Metropolis and university towns.

 

He outlined that these projects aim to bring together quality education and research resources from Hong Kong, the Mainland and overseas to foster the co-ordinated development of education, technology, talent and industries, and to accelerate the commercialisation of research outcomes.

 

He invited Jiangsu enterprises to visit the Northern Metropolis to explore co-operation opportunities.

 

Mr Chan elaborated that, in attracting enterprises and nurturing industries, the Hong Kong SAR Government looks not only at the scale of investments, but also at enterprises’ technological capabilities, capacity for innovation, and long-term contributions to Hong Kong’s I&T ecosystem and talent development.

 

He added that the Hong Kong SAR Government is keen to explore investment co-operation with enterprises that are aligned with Hong Kong’s future development priorities, and to offer support on land, taxation and other areas.

 

He expressed the hope of building long-term partnerships with Jiangsu enterprises and supporting more Mainland enterprises in becoming multinational corporations that have global influence and bring Chinese technologies, products and solutions to markets around the world.

 

Mr Chan also held a breakfast meeting with a group of young Jiangsu entrepreneurs to exchange views on business development and co-operation opportunities between the two places.

 

In addition, he attended a sharing session with Hong Kong business people and enterprises in Jiangsu to learn about their business development in the province.

 

In the afternoon, the delegation visited the National Regional Technology Transfer & Transformation Centre for Higher Education Institutions (Jiangsu) to learn about its work in promoting the transfer and commercialisation of university research outcomes, matching these with the needs of enterprises, and fostering industry-academia-research collaboration.

 

The delegation met officials and representatives from the centre and from Nanjing’s Jiangbei New Area, as well as representatives of local industries and enterprises.

 

They discussed promoting two-way co-operation between Jiangsu and Hong Kong, and establishing more regular mechanisms for I&T collaboration.

 

At the meeting, Mr Chan urged Jiangsu and Hong Kong to strengthen connections among science and technology parks, universities, enterprises, investment institutions and the professional services sector, facilitate talent exchanges, and bring more promising research projects to fruition.

 

In the evening, Mr Chan called on Governor of Jiangsu Province Liu Xiaotao. They discussed deepening economic and trade co-operation between Jiangsu and Hong Kong, connecting innovation and industrial resources, and jointly supporting enterprises in expanding into overseas markets.

title: APEC ministers' meeting opens
body:
The two-day Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Finance Ministers' Meeting 2026 opened in Hong Kong today, marking the first time the city has hosted the event.  

 

Aiming to strengthen regional economic and financial co-operation, participants are discussing the global and regional macroeconomic outlook, fiscal policies supporting households, digital infrastructure financing, financial inclusion and dialogue with financial talent.

 

Speaking at the opening ceremony this morning, Minister of Finance Lan Fo'an noted that a new wave of breakthroughs in technological innovation and industrial transformation is accelerating, gathering new development momentum. He added that as the engine of global economic growth, the Asia-Pacific region bears greater responsibility.

 

Mr Lan said all parties should firmly implement the consensus reached at the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting to contribute to regional prosperity. He urged member economies to strengthen macroeconomic policy dialogue and maintain stability.

 

Given the highly uncertain international economic environment, he advised economies to enhance the soundness of their own policies while boosting communication and co-ordination to prevent negative spillover effects from policy adjustments. He also stressed the need to accelerate economic transformation and enhance resilience by seizing opportunities in digital and green transformation, promoting innovative co-operation in artificial intelligence, the digital economy and green and low-carbon development, and cultivating new growth drivers.

 

Furthermore, he noted that development must remain a priority to promote shared prosperity. Mr Lan urged all economies to deepen practical co-operation in fiscal and financial fields, foster an open regional economic environment, maintain stable supply chains, and advance regional economic integration.

 

Addressing the discussion sessions, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Hong Kong would leverage its unique advantages under the "one country, two systems" principle. He emphasised that the city will make full use of its diverse financing channels and professional services as an international financial centre to serve as a "super connector" and "super value-adder". 

 

He highlighted that by connecting capital, technology and projects across the region, Hong Kong will work with other economies to foster resilient, sustainable and inclusive growth.

 

Chief Executive John Lee officiated at a welcome dinner for delegates this evening. 

 

“Together, we seek to build economies that are more resilient, innovative and inclusive to create continuing opportunities for our businesses, communities and future generations,” he said. 

 

He noted that as a founding member of the World Trade Organization, Hong Kong champions free trade and maintains a zero-tariff policy, a simple and low tax regime, and a predictable business environment, contributing to the city's status as a global financial centre. Mr Lee reiterated the Government’s commitment to strengthening Hong Kong's roles as a global offshore renminbi business hub, an international asset and wealth management centre, and a risk management centre, while advancing commodity trading and green financial services.

 

The Chief Executive pointed out that the Northern Metropolis is fast becoming Hong Kong's new economic engine.

 

“The Northern Metropolis is connected to the enterprising and innovative Mainland city of Shenzhen, where the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting is set to take place next month. It will become an innovation and technology hub and home to three university towns, integrating education, technology and talent,” he said.

 

Mr Lee added that the Northern Metropolis will deepen collaboration within the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area – a cluster city development that brings together Hong Kong, Shenzhen and nine southern cities with a combined gross domestic product that rivals the world's 10th largest economy.
